Bill.BriefDescription: Allowing county registrars to issue certificates of still birth upon the request of the mother or father.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to certificates of still birth; and adding a newsection to chapter 70.58 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.58 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The local registrar of the county in which a stillbirth occursshall issue, upon request of the mother or father of the fetus, acertificate of still birth on a form prescribed by the state registrar.The local registrar must transmit a completed certificate of stillbirth to the state registrar no later than sixty days after itsissuance. (2) Except as otherwise provided in this section, a certificate ofstill birth must comply with all of the format requirements governinga birth certificate. The certificate of still birth is in addition to,and may not replace, a fetal death certificate. (3) A certificate of still birth must contain the followinginformation taken, when possible, from the fetal death certificate: (a) The date of the stillbirth; (b) The county in which the stillbirth occurred; p. 1 HB 1658 (c) The name, if any, and sex of the stillborn fetus; (d) The time and place of the stillbirth, including the streetaddress, and, if applicable, the name of the hospital in which thestillbirth occurred; (e) The names, dates of birth, and states of birth of the motherand father; (f) The file number of the fetal death certificate; (g) A title at the top of the certificate that reads, "Certificateof Still Birth;" and (h) A statement at the bottom of the certificate that reads, "ThisCertificate of Still Birth is not proof of a live birth." (4) The state or local registrar may not use the information on acertificate of still birth for any purpose other than to respond to therequest for the certificate from the mother or father of the fetus. (5) A certificate of still birth must be issued to a mother orfather upon request regardless of the date the fetal death certificatewas issued. (6) The state registrar and the local registrar may charge a feefor processing and issuing a certificate of still birth. The amount ofthe fee may not exceed the full cost of providing the certificate. (7) Nothing in this section may be the basis for a civil cause ofaction seeking damages against any person or entity for bodily injury,personal injury, or wrongful death for a stillbirth. (8) For purposes of this section, "stillbirth" means the deliveryof a fetus where there was a naturally occurring intrauterine fetaldeath after a gestational age of at least twenty completed weeks. (9) Through its statutes, state Constitution, and judicialdecisions, Washington protects a woman's right to reproductive privacyand freedom and it is the intent of legislature to reaffirm thisprotection. Nothing in this section may be interpreted to alter awoman's right to reproductive privacy and freedom in any way or toalter or supersede any other provision of law. The terms used in thissection only apply to this section and do not affect the definition,use, meaning, or intent of the terms as they may appear in any otherstatute, judicial decision, or the state Constitution. Except for theright to request a certificate of still birth, nothing in this section HB 1658 p. 2 constitutes the basis of any new right, privilege, or entitlement orabrogates any existing right, privilege, or entitlement.
